speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you suffered a rear-end collision and now have right groin pain with abnormal leg positioning. Can you tell me exactly how your leg is positioned right now, and did you hear a pop or snap at the time of the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture. The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision with significant force transfer to the pelvis/hips) combined with immediate groin pain and abnormal leg positioning is highly characteristic of a hip fracture. Given the patient's age and the specific location of the pain, this is the primary concern until proven otherwise by imaging.
